intro.data: Encoding here is TWO steps: first Encode the text, then Compress it — that's the only way to reach C. The way back is a single Decode that must undo BOTH steps at once and return the EXACT original. There's no shortcut home from B, so you must encode fully; and among the three decoders, only one truly inverts the pair. Pick the faithful steps and the true decoder.
intro.alchemy: Transmuting here is TWO steps: Transmute the lead, then Condense it — the only path to C. The way back is a single Revert that must undo BOTH and return the EXACT original. There's no shortcut from B, so transmute fully; among the three reverters, only one truly inverts the pair.
intro.spellcraft: Sealing here is TWO steps: Seal the sigil, then Fold it — the only path to C. The way back is a single Unseal that must undo BOTH and return the EXACT original. There's no shortcut from B, so seal fully; among the three unsealings, only one truly inverts the pair.
intro.abstract: g∘f : A → C is a composite isomorphism (A only reaches C via f then g). Its inverse is a single C → A. Build f, g, then the decoder d with d ∘ (g∘f) = id_A; same-typed decoders that don't restore the value fail.

goal.spellcraft: Round-trip the original sigil back to itself.
goal.abstract: Build the round trip returning v-a, inverting g∘f.

afterSuccess.data: You encoded both steps and the single Decode restored the EXACT original — so Decode is the inverse of the whole two-step encoding: d ∘ (g∘f) = id. The inverse of a composite is one arrow that undoes it all. Look-alikes that lost or garbled anything failed.
afterSuccess.alchemy: You transmuted both steps and the single Revert restored the EXACT original: Revert is the inverse of the whole encoding. The inverse of a composite undoes it all at once.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: You sealed both steps and the single Unseal restored the EXACT original: Unseal is the inverse of the whole sealing. The inverse of a composite undoes it all at once.
afterSuccess.abstract: d ∘ (g∘f) = id_A, so d = (g∘f)⁻¹. A composite of isomorphisms is an isomorphism, and one inverse undoes the whole composite.

reveal.summary: If f : A→B and g : B→C are isomorphisms, so is g∘f : A→C, and its inverse is f⁻¹ ∘ g⁻¹ — a single arrow C→A that undoes both steps and restores the original exactly.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: decode(compress(encode(x))) === x — one decoder that reverses the whole pipeline.
